title: the reorder buffer reads a change record it returned to the slab
live_proof: inspection: verified in REL_17_0 with the defect given by line in PROVENANCE.md; nothing is reverted
object: a ReorderBufferChange record from a Slab context
lifetime_ender: ReorderBufferReturnChange puts it back on the slab's LIFO free list
shape: same-address reuse from a fixed-size free list

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: completes with no capability fault; the case's own PG_DEFECT probe prints twice, so the defective sequence provably executed -- REACHED-SILENT (2026-10-05, plain purecap, revocation=1 every_free=0). A use-after-free between two palloc chunks never crosses a malloc boundary, so there is nothing for a malloc-granular revoker to reclaim.
cheribsd-revocation.run: 2026-10-05, CheriBSD riscv64-purecap, built via PG_CORPUS_DIR through ports/postgres/memory-contexts with PG_POISONCAP off

status: poisoncap-spatial and poisoncap-protected run 2026-09-20 under QEMU against the mmap-backed adapter; mode 0 completed and mode 1 faulted at the labelled probe, address matched. The Capstone spatial/sublet arms have NOT been run since the corpus was split into one program per case.
nested_why: The object comes from PostgreSQL's own memory manager -- a chunk aset.c or slab.c carved out of a block it took from malloc -- so the defect is nested by the allocator that served it.
